setup_summary.text: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 27) was a much cleaner print than the year-ago quarter, which carried the $4.9B 777X charge. Revenue was $24.19B (+3.9%), operating income $354M (1.5% margin) and diluted EPS -$0.26 versus -$7.14. Core EPS was -$0.34. The business is still loss-making at the bottom line: nine-month net loss attributable to shareholders was $564M.

Against expectations the quarter missed. Core EPS of -$0.34 compared with an LSEG consensus of -$0.21, the second straight EPS miss. Boeing has beaten once and missed three times over the last four quarters, with an average surprise of -75.9%. A StockStory item called the quarter 'in line', so the characterization depends on the basis used.

Free cash flow is the central number. Q3 FCF was +$464M after about $700M of DOJ payments, but nine-month FCF is -$359M. Management narrowed 2026 FCF to about $2B, which implies roughly $2.4B in Q4. That compares with only about +$0.37B in Q4 2025 (FY2025 FCF -$1.88B less nine-month -$2.25B). The $2B assumes the KC-46A Lot 13 order comes in advance and seasonal working-capital benefits.

New multiyear FCF targets reset the debate: about $3B in 2027, about $6B in 2028 and $10B in 2029, assuming 777X certification by mid-2027. The CEO called it 'almost a one-year shift to the right'. Jefferies cited Street 2027 consensus FCF of about $5.5B before the call, so the 2027 figure is a large shortfall.

Operational overhangs entering Q4: 737 stabilization at rate 47 slipped into 2027 (wings are the pacing item), the 500-jet 737 delivery target will be missed, and 787 deliveries are guided to the low end of 90-100. A supplier parts shortage is disrupting the 777 Freighter and 767/KC-46A lines into 2027. 777X certification flight testing still needs FAA approval for the balance of the program, including ETOPS. The 737-7 and 737-10 are now certified.

Q4 consensus (report expected 2027-01-25, after the close) is EPS of $0.04 on revenue of $27.25B, which is +13.8% revenue growth. The year-ago Q4 EPS of $10.73 included a $9.67B gain on dispositions, mostly the Digital Aviation Solutions sale, so the EPS comparison is not meaningful.

Balance sheet is improving but still leveraged. Debt was $45.9B (down from $54.1B at year-end), cash and marketable securities $20.7B, and $10B of revolvers are undrawn. Ratings are BBB-/Baa3 with stable outlooks (Fitch outlook positive). Net debt was $25.2B.

Peer read-across: Airbus has delivered 547 aircraft year to date versus Boeing's 475. It reaffirmed about 870 for 2026, which needs about 323 in Q4 (about 108 per month). Airbus Q3 EBIT adjusted fell 9% on lower deliveries and mix. Airframer ramp skepticism is rising, per RBC.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 revenue was $24.19B, up 3.9% year on year.

consensus.text: Q4 consensus revenue is $27.25B, +13.8% against $23.95B a year earlier and about +12.7% sequentially from Q3.

view.text: Consensus looks demanding. If BDS and BGS hold near their Q3 run-rate ($9.5B and $5.6B, an assumption), $27.25B implies BCA revenue of roughly $13.7B. That is about 28% above Q3's $10.72B and about 20% above Q4 2025's $11.4B on 160 deliveries. 737 output is capped below roughly 133 units (500 target missed, 367 delivered year to date) and 787 implies about 28-38 units. Prebuilt -7/-10s cannot deliver until early 2027. Consensus may not have fully reset after Oct 27, so revenue risk skews to the downside.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 diluted EPS was -$0.26 (GAAP) and core EPS -$0.34, with net loss attributable to shareholders of $116M.

view.text: $0.03 on about 793M diluted shares is roughly $24M to common after $87M of preferred dividends, i.e. about $110M of net income attributable, versus Q3's -$116M loss. Q3 also included a $252M HRL gain that will not repeat, so the underlying swing needed is about $0.5B of pre-tax improvement. That comes against guided abnormal supplier costs at BCA in Q4. A miss is the more likely direction, consistent with 3 misses in 4 quarters.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 BCA deliveries were 161 (737: 124, 767: 10, 777: 5, 787: 22); nine-month deliveries were 475. Q4 2025 was 160 (737: 117, 787: 27, 777: 6, 767: 10), derived from FY2025 less nine months.

view.text: 737 Q4 deliveries must come in below about 133 for the year to miss 500, versus 124 in Q3. The 787 guide of 90-100, closer to the low end, implies about 28-38 against 62 year to date, a likely low-end outcome. A Q4 total roughly in the 160s-170s is plausible, but only modest growth over Q4 2025. American Airlines says it expects no further Boeing deliveries this year. Program detail for 2027 (BCA deliveries +10% or more) comes in January.

last_reported.text: Q3 BCA operating margin was -6.5% ($697M loss), versus -48.3% a year earlier with the 777X charge; nine-month margin was -5.0%.

view.text: No 777X-style charge is expected, but abnormal costs from the 777F/767 supplier disruption will be period-expensed in Q4 and through 1H27. Lower booking rates from the delayed 737 and 787 rate steps persist. Management points to about breakeven in early 2028 and a significant improvement only later. Expect Q4 BCA margin to stay negative, near Q3's level. Further reach-forward or EAC changes are the tail risk.

last_reported.text: Q3 BDS operating margin was 6.2% ($492M on $7.94B revenue), including a $252M gain on the sale of HRL Laboratories. Excluding the gain it was about 3.0%. Revenue rose 15%.

view.text: Model BDS margin from the roughly 3% underlying base, not 6.2%. Management targets steady improvement toward high-single digits by the end of the decade. Fixed-price development programs (VC-25B added $312M of losses year to date; KC-46A is suffering supplier-driven abnormal costs) remain sources of Q4 catch-up charges.

last_reported.text: Q3 FCF was +$464M; nine-month FCF was -$359M (operating cash flow $2.68B less capex $3.04B).

view.text: Hitting about $2B for the year needs about $2.4B in Q4, roughly six times Q4 2025's derived +$0.37B. It leans on the KC-46A Lot 13 order arriving in advance, seasonal working capital and customer deposits. A government funding lapse after Dec 11, a slipped Lot 13 award or weak December deliveries are the main misses. Whether Q4 lands near $2B is the key credibility test for the new 2027-29 targets.

last_reported.text: Nine-month 2026 capex was $3.04B (+53%); Q3 capex was $1.03B.

view.text: 2027 capex is guided to about $5B, about $1B above 2026, which implies about $4B for 2026 and about $1B in Q4. 2028 and 2029 are about $4B a year, normalizing at 3-4% of revenue versus about 2% historically.

last_reported.text: Total backlog was a record $745.4B (BCA $611.8B, BDS $100.5B, BGS $32.7B). Nine-month BCA cancellations were $3.2B and net ASC 606 adjustments -$1.9B.

view.text: The F/A-XX award is not in Q3 backlog pending source selection, so BDS backlog could step up if it is booked in Q4. BCA order deposits and net orders should stay strong (2026 is trending to a record year for deposits), but cancellations and ASC 606 write-downs are the offset to watch.

guidance.guidance: About $2B (narrowed). Includes assumption of the KC-46A Lot 13 order in advance and seasonal working capital benefits.

claim.text: Management narrowed 2026 FCF to about $2B, assuming KC-46A Lot 13 comes in advance. Press reports described the prior range as $1-3B, which is not in the filings, so the direction is unclear (midpoint-ish). Against -$359M year to date it implies about $2.4B in Q4.

guidance.guidance: About $3B, assuming 777X certified by mid-2027; DOJ payment (~$700M) does not repeat; lower BCA deposits (a few billion) and about $1B more capex offset.

claim.text: First 2027 FCF target is about $3B, versus Street FCF of about $5.5B (Jefferies). Management says 777X certification by mid-2027 is assumed, and a one-to-two-month slip can be absorbed.

guidance.guidance: About $6B in 2028; $10B in 2029, with significant growth beyond 2029.

claim.text: The $10B target is now dated 2029. The CEO called the path 'almost a one-year shift to the right' with the endpoint unchanged, and Reuters noted it is a year later than consensus. The 2029 building blocks are 737 deliveries in the mid-to-high 50s, about 12 per month on the 787 and positive 777X cash.

guidance.guidance: About $5B in 2027; about $4B per year in 2028 and 2029; 3-4% of revenue normalized.

claim.text: First quantified capex outlook. The 10-Q previously only said 2026 capex would exceed 2025's $2.94B.

guidance.guidance: 500-delivery target will be missed. Stabilization at rate 47 now expected in 2027; financial plan targets rate 52 in 2H27.

claim.text: As recently as May, executives said rate 47 would be reached this summer. The CFO said 2026 737 deliveries will fall shy of 500, and the 10-Q moved stabilization into 2027. Rate 52 in 2H27 requires the North Line to be FAA production-certified and stable wings and Wichita fuselages.

guidance.guidance: 90-100 deliveries, closer to the low end; transition to rate 10 to begin in December 2026; engines are the pacing item.

claim.text: The range is unchanged but leans low because rate 10 is delayed. Nine-month deliveries were 62, so Q4 implies 28-38.

guidance.guidance: First 777-9 delivery in 2027; production about one per month for most of 2027; assumptions within the EAC reset last year.

claim.text: Timing is maintained, though flight-test authorization for the balance of the program including ETOPS is still outstanding. Program cash is a significant use in 2027, improves in 2028 and turns positive in 2029.

guidance.guidance: Up 10% or more in 2027, with about 30 prebuilt 737-7/-10 aircraft delivering. Program detail in January.

claim.text: This is the first 2027 delivery framing. Detail by program is promised for the Q4 report, which is the main read-through event in the next print.

guidance.guidance: Abnormal supplier costs pressure margins in Q4 and 1H27. About breakeven in early 2028. 737 will not return to 2018 margins; 787 exceeds them by 2029.

claim.text: Management ties the disruption to the 777F/767 lines and expects it to fade after 1H27.

guidance.guidance: Mid-single-digit-or-higher revenue growth (versus low single digits thought a year ago); steady margin improvement toward high-single digits by end of decade.

claim.text: The CEO said defense growth should be higher than the low-single-digit rate previously assumed, moving toward high-middle-single-digit or higher. He cited F-15EX, PAC-3 Seeker and the F/A-XX selection. The CFO said Boeing remains confident in a path to high-single-digit BDS operating margins by the end of the decade. The CEO said NGAD is cost-plus. On F/A-XX he said only that he could not say and that it is an appropriate contract type.

since_filing.text: The call (Oct 27, same day as the 10-Q) contradicts the filing on one point. The CEO said 'through the third quarter, we delivered 161 commercial aircraft'. The 10-Q shows 161 was Q3 deliveries alone (nine-month total 475). The filing figure is reported and prevails; the 'most since 2018' claim cannot be checked.

Tension on BCA profitability: the CFO referred to BCA margins being about breakeven for 2026 (a reference to Q2 commentary), while the 10-Q shows a nine-month BCA operating margin of -5.0% and Q3 of -6.5%. The 777 and 777X are near break-even gross margin. The basis of the breakeven remark (cash or gross) is unclear, and the filing is the more reliable tier.

Sell-side reaction after Q3: price targets were cut (Morgan Stanley $225 to $195, Baird $300 to $230, TD Cowen $240 to $210, JPMorgan $290 to $240, Bernstein $278 to $223, Susquehanna $285 to $250, BofA $270 to $235). Citi kept Buy and $260. Ratings were largely maintained. JPMorgan said the FY27-29 targets are meaningfully below consensus but look more achievable. Consensus target is $243.73, +42.1% versus $171.55.

Estimate resets: 2027 EPS consensus was cited at about $3.48 versus $6.46 a year ago, with a MarketBeat tally of 1 Strong Buy, 22 Buy, 7 Hold and 3 Sell. The Q4 consensus in the report calendar ($0.03 EPS, $27.25B revenue) may predate the Oct 27 reset.

Newsflow since the filing: the FAA type certificate for the 737 MAX 10 is dated Oct 20, and the first MAX 10 off the new Everett North Line rolled out Oct 26. A Reuters-reported supplier dispute stalled wing production for 777 freighters and 767/KC-46A, with shipments resumed and the impact flowing over the next few quarters.

Airbus (Oct 28-29) reaffirmed about 870 deliveries, needing about 323 in Q4, after Q3 EBIT adjusted fell 9% to EUR1.77B and revenue fell 2%. Its CEO said it is 'no longer' in the slower ramp situation. Boeing trails on year-to-date deliveries, 475 versus 547.

Supply-chain read-across: GE Aerospace raised 2026 guidance (adjusted EPS $8.00-8.10, FCF $9.1-9.4B), but LEAP deliveries grew only about 5% in Q3 versus +26% year to date. GE says supply constraints will continue to affect production. Honeywell Aerospace sales grew 2% on parts shortages and its shares fell 11%.

key_debates.question: Are the 2027-29 FCF targets (about $3B/$6B/$10B) credible, or is another slip coming?

bull.text: Management says the range of outcomes is narrowing. The record $894B backlog carries improved pricing, fixed-price development risk is largely reset, and 777X slippage of a month or two is absorbable. JPMorgan calls the new targets more achievable even though they sit below consensus.

bear.text: The 2027 target is well below the prior $5.5B Street view, the 737 rate-47 date already slipped from summer 2026 to 2027, and the plan assumes 777X certification by mid-2027 with the ETOPS flight-test authorization not yet in hand. Inventory grew to $90.9B and 737 deferred production costs to $14.0B.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 FCF versus the about $2.4B implied, the January 2027 delivery guide by program, and 777X flight-test authorization progress.

key_debates.question: Can the 737 get to a stable rate 47 and then rate 52 in 2H27?

bull.text: Final-assembly rework is down 40% since the start of last year, the 737-7 and -10 are certified, the North Line is rolling out its first MAX 10, and management is deliberately holding at 47 rather than rushing.

bear.text: Wing back-shop flow enablers did not deliver the expected savings, Wichita fuselages are intentionally below final-assembly rate and must ramp, and the North Line still needs FAA production certification. RBC flags growing skepticism on airframer ramp targets.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Monthly 737 delivery cadence in Q4, whether wing output is demonstrated stable, FAA certification of the North Line, and the 737 rate timing in the January call.

key_debates.question: When does BCA profitability inflect given supplier cost pressure and delayed rate steps?

bull.text: Management sees a higher-priced backlog, cost-based extensions and higher volume lifting margins to about breakeven in early 2028, with 787 margins above 2018 levels by 2029. The Q3 EAC changes are already in the cash projections.

bear.text: Q3 BCA margin was -6.5% on lower booking rates and higher supply chain cost estimates, new abnormal costs hit Q4 and 1H27, and the 777X program remains a significant 2027 cash use. The 737 will not regain 2018 margins.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q4 BCA operating margin and the size of abnormal costs, plus any EAC or reach-forward changes disclosed in the 10-K.

key_debates.question: Is BDS earnings power improving, or flattered by one-offs?

bull.text: BDS revenue grew 15%. F/A-XX, PAC-3 and F-15EX wins and fixed-price milestones (MQ-25 and T-7A at Milestone C) support mid-single-digit-plus growth and a margin path to high-single digits.

bear.text: The 6.2% Q3 margin included a $252M gain, so the underlying margin was about 3%. VC-25B added $312M of losses this year, KC-46A faces abnormal supplier-driven costs, and the Starliner schedule slipped to 2027-28.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 BDS margin ex-gains, any new reach-forward charges, and the F/A-XX booking and contract structure.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Q4 delivers on the ~$2B FCF guide (about $2.4B in the quarter), driven by KC-46A Lot 13 and strong deposits. 737 deliveries come in near the top of the feasible range, 787 deliveries meet the low end of the range, and BCA abnormal costs stay contained. EPS lands at or above $0.03 on better BDS and BGS. January color supports the 777X and 2027 delivery assumptions. The stock rebounds as the post-Q3 de-rating reverses.

triggers: Q4 FCF at or above about $2.4B
FAA authorizes the remaining 777X flight-test phases including ETOPS
F/A-XX booked in backlog with a favorable contract type
2027 deliveries guided up 10% or more with a clear rate-52 path

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Q4 FCF lands near but slightly short of the ~$2B full-year target, helped by year-end working capital. Revenue is below the $27.25B consensus (BCA constrained at about 160-175 deliveries). BCA remains loss-making near Q3's margin on abnormal costs. BDS is back to about a 3% margin without the HRL gain, so EPS is around breakeven, below $0.03. January reaffirms the 2027-29 targets with more detail, and the print is judged on cash and the delivery guide rather than the EPS miss.

triggers: FCF between $1.5B and $2.2B for the year
Full-year deliveries about 640-650 given 475 year to date (illustrative)

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: The KC-46A Lot 13 advance or customer deposits slip, or a government funding lapse after Dec 11 delays payments, leaving FY2026 FCF well below $2B. The supplier disruption widens abnormal costs. 737 and 787 deliveries miss, and a new EAC or reach-forward charge hits BCA or BDS. The 777X slips beyond mid-2027, challenging the $3B 2027 FCF target. EPS misses for a fourth time in five quarters.

triggers: New reach-forward loss on a fixed-price or 777X program
Ratings outlook change or financing commitments drawn

claim.text: Supplier parts shortage that began in Q3 is disrupting the 777 Freighter and 767/KC-46A lines. It is expected to continue into 2027, with abnormal production costs expensed as incurred. The Q3 cost was not material.

737 rate-ramp risk: wing back-shop flow enablers underdelivered, Wichita fuselages must resync with final assembly, and the North Line needs FAA production certification. Management says the delay adversely affects financial position and cash flows.

777X certification and cash: first delivery in 2027 depends on FAA approval of the remaining flight-test phases (ETOPS) and a supplier fix for the engine durability issue. 777X work in process rose to $7.6B from $4.3B, and the program is a significant 2027 cash use. The FCF plan assumes mid-2027 certification.
U.S. government agencies are funded only through Dec 11, 2026, so a lapse or continuing resolution is a Q4 risk to BDS and BGS cash timing and FAA activity. The FY27 NASA request is $6B below FY26.

Fixed-price development exposure persists: VC-25B added $312M of losses in 2026, KC-46A faces abnormal supplier costs, Starliner slipped to an uncrewed mission in Q1 2027 with crewed flights late 2028, and each program carries 'risk remains that we may record additional losses'.

Macro and fuel: elevated fuel prices could soften growth orders. Management has seen no customer replan and says replacement demand and an oversold backlog give room to re-sequence. It did not state the oil price assumed in the FCF targets.

Leverage and financing exposure: debt of $45.9B with BBB-/Baa3 ratings, $16.5B of financing commitments of which $11.3B relate to below-investment-grade customers with no reserve, and ULA support (a $750M guarantee, with more support expected in Q4 while Vulcan launches are paused).

The 10-Q states no material changes to 10-K risk factors. SPEEA contracts were ratified Oct 1, removing the October 2026 labor expiration flagged in the 10-K, while IAM contract expirations remain in 2027-2030.

questions_for_management.question: What gives you confidence in about $2.4B of Q4 FCF, and how much depends on the KC-46A Lot 13 advance and year-end deposits versus operations?

why.text: Nine-month FCF is -$359M and the $2B target assumes the Lot 13 order in advance; Q4 2025 was only about +$0.37B.

questions_for_management.question: What are Q4 and 2027 deliveries by program (737, 787, 777, 767), and how many -7/-10 units will deliver in Q1 versus later?

why.text: Management promised program detail in January; 737 will miss 500, the 787 is guided to the low end, and about 30 prebuilt -7/-10 aircraft deliver in 2027.

questions_for_management.question: How large are the abnormal costs from the 777F/767/KC-46A supplier disruption by quarter, and when will the supplier return to normal output?

why.text: Q3 cost was said to be not material but will be expensed over the next few quarters, pressuring BCA margins through 1H27.

questions_for_management.question: What is the evidence that 737 wing output is stable at rate 47 today, and what are the gating milestones for North Line certification and rate 52?

why.text: Flow enablers did not yield the expected savings; rate 47 stability slipped into 2027, and rate 52 is planned for 2H27.

questions_for_management.question: What FAA authorizations remain for 777X flight testing (including ETOPS), and what is the engine durability fix timeline?

why.text: FCF targets assume mid-2027 certification; management said it still needs approval for the balance of flight testing and is working the engine issue with the supplier.

questions_for_management.question: What assumptions underlie the $3B 2027 FCF target on deposits, working capital, 737/787 cash margins and fuel prices, and what is the sensitivity to a 777X slip beyond mid-2027?

why.text: The bridge involves a few billion dollars of lower deposits and $1B more capex; analysts noted ex-DOJ growth is only a few hundred million dollars; management did not say what oil price is assumed.

questions_for_management.question: What is the F/A-XX contract structure and development capex, and do you expect additional reach-forward exposure on fixed-price development programs?

why.text: Management called F/A-XX 'appropriate' without specifying fixed price; 2027 capex includes F/A-XX development and VC-30B and KC-46A continue to see charges.

data_gaps: Whether the Q4 consensus EPS of $0.03 is on a GAAP or core basis is not stated, and the Q3 miss was measured against core EPS. The consensus date (before or after the Oct 27 reset) is also unknown.
No consensus figures for Q4 BCA deliveries, segment revenue or margins, free cash flow or capex were found. The 2027 FCF consensus of about $5.5B is from a single Jefferies note in press reports.
The prior 2026 FCF range ($1-3B) appears only in press reports, not in the filings, so the direction of the 'narrowing' cannot be confirmed from primary sources.
The next report date (2027-01-25) is from a calendar; EarningsWatcher has no confirmed date, so options-implied move and whisper EPS are unavailable. The report is about 85 days away.
The full call transcript date is not stated in the source; the Reuters report places the call on Oct 27, 2026.

The 777X 2027 delivery count is not explicitly guided in the transcript. Reuters reports '10 to 15 deliveries next year', but the CFO's wording ties 10-15 to the deliveries at risk if certification slips later in the year.
The oil price assumed in the FCF targets, the magnitude of Q4 abnormal costs, and the timing and size of the KC-46A Lot 13 advance are not disclosed.

The Q4 2025 comparison is distorted by the $9.57B Digital Aviation Solutions gain, so there is no clean year-over-year EPS base. Q4 2025 segment revenue and deliveries are derived from FY2025 less nine months.

A news item on a securities-fraud probe tied to the MAX 10 delay (appears to be a law-firm notice, with unclear dating) was not used. Airbus is not an SEC filer, so peer figures are from press and release summaries only.
Spirit purchase accounting is still preliminary (goodwill $10.6B), so segment results could be revised before finalization within one year of Dec 8, 2025.

A claim was removed because its sources don't support it: "Shares fell 9.6% to $170.23 in afternoon trading on Oct 27, which Reuters said would be the stock's worst day since April 3, 2025. The stock hit a fresh 18-month low, reported on Oct 29, and was $171.55 at the data cut. Reuters tied the day's news to free cash flow, with $464 million in the quarter and $359 million burned year to date, and to the 737 rate slip: 47 a month now expected in early 2027, and the 500-delivery target missed. The average closing move over the last eight reports was ±3.8%." (The passages give 47 jets a month in early 2027, but nothing says the stock was $171.55 at the data cut beyond market data, and the Oct 27 date for the 9.6% drop is not in the passages (the call is described as Tuesday, with no date); the 18-month low is reported by TradingView on Oct 29 without a link to Reuters' FCF framing.  More importantly, the "reported on Oct 29" and "Oct 27" dates are not stated for the share drop in the Reuters passage.</br>).
